index.041: The cloud you already use, in FileDesk
index.042: Sign in to the official Google Drive for desktop, OneDrive, pCloud or Dropbox sync app. FileDesk finds and opens its sync folder. This is the recommended approach for most users, with no separate authorization or direct-login user limit.
index.043: Advanced: You can also sign in directly through your browser in FileDesk, without the official sync app, to browse folders and upload or download files. Direct connections are managed separately from the sync app.
index.044: Login credentials are stored encrypted on your computer. Cloud files travel between your device and your chosen service, without passing through a FileDesk-operated server. Read our privacy policy for details.
index.045: Google Drive direct login (advanced) is awaiting public verification.
index.046: The Google authentication app is in production. Until public verification is complete, an unverified-app notice and user limits remain. Current Mac installers include browser-based Google login; older installations need to be updated. Sign in again if the provider revokes access or requires reauthentication.
index.048: For FileDesk development or support inquiries, email ifreemumu@gmail.com. Do not send login tokens or passwords.

guide.023: Open the folders you need side by side.
guide.024: Icon view on the left, list view on the right. The highlighted border marks the active pane. Click the image to enlarge
guide.025: Choose a horizontal, vertical or four-pane arrangement in Layout. There are 13 layouts with up to six panes.
guide.026: Click a pane, then choose a folder from Favorites or Locations. Other panes keep their current locations.
guide.027: Drag a divider to resize the panes. Double-click it to restore the default proportions.
guide.028: Drag the dotted handle at the top onto another pane to swap positions. Use Close Pane in the pane menu to reduce the pane count.
guide.029: Try four panes when reviewing and organizing files together. Click the image to enlarge
guide.031: Add a tab with ＋ at the top of a pane or ⌘T. Each tab can open a different folder. Click an ancestor in the path bar to jump there. Click the current folder name or empty path space, or press ⌘L, to type a path. Back, Forward and the parent-folder menu are also available.
guide.033: Temporary shelf: collect first, organize together.
guide.034: Collect files scattered across folders without moving the originals, then copy them together to your destination.
guide.035: The shelf is at the bottom in FileDesk style. Drag its top edge to adjust its height; double-click to restore the default. Click the image to enlarge
guide.037: Drag files onto the shelf, or copy files and choose Paste Files. You can also choose Add to Temporary Shelf from the selected files’ context menu. Folders are excluded. To save a clipboard image as a file, click a pane or the shelf and press ⌘V.
guide.039: Click the receiving pane and open the destination folder. Check its highlighted border.
guide.041: Choose Save to Current Folder to copy all shelf items into the selected local folder. You can also drag individual items out to a folder.
guide.042: “Clear Shelf List” does not delete originals.
guide.043: It only clears the list. The shelf is not a separate backup: removing the original or disconnecting its external drive makes it unavailable. The list survives app restarts.
guide.044: Open a small independent window with Tools → Floating Shelf on the left. In Settings, choose Icons + Names or Icons Only for shelf buttons. The bottom shelf is hidden in Finder and Windows Explorer styles.
guide.047: Open the preview pane with the file information button. Click the image to enlarge
guide.048: Choose Icon, List, Column or Gallery view with each pane’s view controls. Images, video, music and documents use thumbnails supported by macOS; unsupported formats show their file icons.
guide.049: Preview pane: Select a file and enable the top file information button or … → Preview Options → Preview Pane.
guide.050: Video and music: Use a supported file’s play button or right-click Play to play inside FileDesk. MP4, MOV, MP3, MKV, WebM and AVI are supported. Formats such as MKV are converted during playback, so seeking is limited to the converted portion. Files that cannot play open in an installed player such as IINA or VLC. On network drives such as WebDAV, file-type icons appear first; image and video thumbnails fill in afterward.
guide.051: Quick Look: Select a file and press Space or choose Quick Look. For SRT subtitles, the preview shows timecodes and text. Use the arrow keys to browse files.
guide.052: Folder status: Icons and item counts distinguish empty folders from folders containing files.
guide.054: Copy and search in the active pane.
guide.055: Right-clicking a file and clicking the pane’s … button open the same action menu. Check the active pane’s border and selected files before acting.
guide.057: Create files and folders; copy, move, duplicate, drag and drop, or move items to Trash. FileDesk style provides top Copy, Paste and Move buttons. Name conflicts prompt you for an action. Dragging follows Finder: move on the same disk, copy across disks; hold ⌥ to copy or ⌘ to move. Trash confirmation is off by default; enable Confirm Before Moving to Trash in the File menu. Undo supported local operations with ⌘Z and redo with ⇧⌘Z. Up to 30 history steps survive app restarts.
guide.059: Press ⌘F to search the current local pane by name or tag, with multiple terms and !excluded terms. Enable Include Subfolders in the search icon menu to search below the current folder. In … → Sort By, choose name, modification date, size, kind or descending order. Enable Folders First to separate folders.
guide.060: Use Use Groups and Group By to group by kind, name, date or size. Enable View Options → Show Hidden Files to reveal hidden items. Connected cloud and FTP/SFTP panes focus on remote browsing, name search, uploads and downloads.
guide.063: Review proposed names before applying changes. Click the image to enlarge
guide.064: Select multiple files and choose Rename, or … → More Actions → Advanced Batch Rename. Combine a base name, prefix, suffix, find/replace/remove, regular expressions, numbering and digit count, modification date and letter case. Save and reload frequently used rules.
guide.065: Rename one file with <kbd>F2</kbd>. Depending on your Mac’s function-key settings, you may also need <kbd>fn</kbd>.
guide.067: Tags, folder colors and center images.
guide.069: Right-click a file and select a circular color tag. Multiple colors can be applied; selected tags show ✓. A tag present on only some selected files shows −; clicking applies it to the whole selection. Browse tagged files by color from the left sidebar.
guide.070: FileDesk uses Finder’s tag metadata, so Finder changes are reflected too. File-system and search-index updates may take time.
guide.071: Several tags applied to one file. Click the image to enlarge
guide.073: Right-click folders and choose Folder Color → Custom Color…. Use Open Color Picker…, choose a color and click Apply. Eight presets and a default reset are available; apply to several folders at once.
guide.074: Choose a color, then Apply to save. Click the image to enlarge
guide.075: Choose from the color wheel, palettes or RGB sliders. Click the image to enlarge
guide.076: Place an image in the folder’s center
guide.077: Choose ICNS (Mac), ICO (Windows), PNG or another image using Folder Image → Choose Image File…. Use Paste Image for a copied image or icon file.
guide.078: The folder outline stays intact, with the image centered on its front. Transparency is preserved without a white square backing; empty areas show the folder color. A subtle shadow follows the image shape. Remove Inserted Image removes only the center image. Folder colors and images are FileDesk display settings, separate from Finder tags.
guide.079: A small center image keeps the folder shape visible. Click the image to enlarge
guide.080: Right-click a Favorite to set its icon and text colors separately or remove a custom Favorite.
guide.083: In FileDesk style, open Settings with the gear button to choose a theme and System, Light or Dark mode. Use the buttons below to compare real theme screenshots.
guide.092: Blue theme · Click the image to enlarge
guide.094: Open the macOS color picker from Custom Color in Settings. The choice is saved, with accent brightness adjusted for legibility in light and dark modes. Sidebar text stays black in light mode and white in dark mode.
guide.095: Theme color and appearance mode can be chosen independently. Click the image to enlarge
guide.097: Choose FileDesk, Finder or Windows Explorer style in View → Finder Style. All styles support split panes and tabs. The FileDesk toolbar and bottom shelf appear only in FileDesk style. Windows Explorer style adds file and folder counts and remaining space at the bottom.
guide.098: In Settings, choose Icons + Names or Icons Only and save each toolbar button’s visibility. Menus support Korean, English, Japanese, German, French, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.
guide.100: Connected drives, in the active pane.
guide.102: First click the pane that should show the drive.
guide.103: Sign in to the official Google Drive, OneDrive, pCloud or Dropbox sync app.
guide.104: Choose the detected sync folder under Cloud Connections on the left. If it is missing, choose Scan Again or specify the folder manually.
guide.105: Opening it shows files and folders in the selected main pane. The official app manages syncing.
guide.106: Without a sync app, choose a provider in Advanced: Direct Login… → Add Account… and complete consent with Sign In with Browser. Reopen direct accounts from the sidebar.
guide.107: Settings manage connections; panes handle files, navigation, uploads and downloads. Account credentials are encrypted locally and not deleted for temporary connection errors. Sign in again if the provider revokes access or requires reauthentication.
guide.109: The Connect Dropbox… button also starts browser login. Sign in and consent without registering authentication keys; the account opens in the active pane. The default personal space is supported.
guide.110: Click the receiving pane and open Server Connections on the left.
guide.111: Enter protocol, address, username and other server details. For SFTP, leaving the password blank uses Terminal’s SSH configuration: host aliases in ~/.ssh/config, the SSH agent and keys. You can also select a private key.
guide.112: Browse server folders in the selected pane. Save address profiles if needed; passwords are excluded.
guide.113: macOS mounts SMB, WebDAV, NFS and AFP as volumes. FTP, FTPS and SFTP support remote file and folder uploads and downloads. The status bar shows progress, transferred data, time remaining and cancellation. Items transfer in parallel (adjust concurrency in Settings → Transfers); copies within one cloud account run on the provider’s server. Resend interrupted items to continue with remaining files. SFTP checks saved server keys. Server deletions cannot be recovered with Trash or Undo.
guide.115: The authentication app is in production, but public verification is unfinished; unverified-app notices and user limits may remain. OneDrive and pCloud availability depends on the account and service policy. Connected clouds, iCloud Drive, servers and running share servers appear under Locations. Set up new accounts under Connections using Cloud Connections, Server Connections, Share Server or Taildrop. Right-click a location to Rename… its display label (blank restores the default) or Disconnect…. Provider files and official-app logins stay intact. Cloud services use provider icons; NAS devices use manufacturer icons such as Synology. Drag between cloud, server and local panes to copy. If a cloud or server is involved, only copying is supported and originals remain.
guide.117: Send to your other devices with Taildrop.
guide.118: Send selected files from your Mac to your devices connected through Tailscale, including Windows PCs.
guide.120: Install Tailscale on the sending Mac and receiving device, sign in with your own account and connect both.
guide.121: Make sure Send Files is enabled in General settings of the Tailscale admin console.
guide.122: Taildrop currently works between your own personal devices. Other users’ devices and tagged devices are restricted. In Settings under Transfers, you can choose separately whether Taildrop and LocalSend appear in the sidebar.
guide.125: Select files or folders to send.
guide.126: Right-click Send with Taildrop… or choose Taildrop on the left.
guide.127: Choose an online device from Receiving Device. Use Choose Files… to change the selection if needed.
guide.128: Click Send and check completion. Find received files in Tailscale on the receiving device.
guide.129: Start directly from a selected file’s context menu. Click the image to enlarge
guide.131: Folders are sent as ZIP archives. File and outgoing ZIP names are normalized to composed Unicode to reduce separated Korean consonants and vowels. Original names are unchanged. Paths inside ZIPs and the receiving app’s behavior are separate concerns.
guide.132: If no device appears, check both connections and Send Files, then Refresh. FileDesk shows only devices Tailscale allows to receive files. Taildrop is separate from FileDesk cloud account connections.
guide.134: The sidebar’s AirDrop opens Finder’s AirDrop screen. Select files or folders and use AirDrop or the sharing menu to open the macOS transfer sheet for nearby Apple devices.
guide.137: Select files and choose Compress to create ZIP or TAR.GZ archives. Browse or search an archive’s contents and extract everything. Korean ZIP names, app-internal links and executable permissions, and single GZ/BZ2 extraction are supported. Some encrypted or damaged formats may not be supported.
guide.141: Pane layouts and folder locations restore automatically. Use Save Current Layout on the left to name a workspace and reopen frequently used combinations.
guide.143: Use the pane’s … menu or right-click a path to copy the current folder path or paths of multiple selected items. Choose Open Terminal in Current Folder to start there.
guide.145: Open Find Duplicates, Compare Documents or Compare Folders from Tools on the left. Review results before acting; folder comparison can copy missing items. Calculate SHA-256 from More Actions in the File menu.
guide.147: Eject external drives, installer disk images and network volumes using the eject button. System and internal disks are excluded. The Go menu includes standard locations, 15 recent folders, parent folder, startup disk and path entry.

privacy.006: This policy applies to direct cloud connections in the FileDesk desktop app and to this introduction website. FileDesk is a file manager that lets users browse and transfer their own files.
privacy.008: When you choose a cloud connection and approve the provider’s consent screen, FileDesk reads file-list metadata such as file and folder names, identifiers, paths, types, sizes and modification dates. Downloads and uploads read or transfer the selected file content; creating a folder creates it at the provider. Account and drive information needed to choose storage, such as shared drives, may also be processed.
privacy.009: Google Drive requests the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive scope. This allows viewing, editing, creating and deleting Drive files. The current interface supports browsing, downloading, uploading, creating folders, and renaming or deleting selected items. Restoration depends on the provider’s trash policy. Without permission, direct Google Drive access is unavailable; local file features remain usable.
privacy.011: Passwords are entered on the provider’s browser login page; FileDesk does not receive them directly. OAuth access and refresh tokens are encrypted in the computer’s app-data area to maintain the connection. On macOS, the encryption key is kept in Keychain. Account labels and connection settings are stored locally. Downloaded files remain in the folder you select.
privacy.012: FileDesk’s operator does not collect cloud files or login tokens on a separate server. Uploads and downloads go directly between your device and the provider through the bundled rclone connection engine.
privacy.014: Google API information is used only for user-facing file browsing and transfers. It is not used for targeted advertising, data sales, lending or credit assessments, or training general-purpose AI models. Cloud files are not provided to advertisers, data brokers or analytics companies. FileDesk’s operator does not read users’ cloud files.
privacy.015: If you explicitly send a downloaded file to another server, cloud or device, it is transferred to that destination. FileDesk sends only files required for that operation to the destination you specify. Google, Microsoft, pCloud and other selected providers apply their own policies to login, storage and processing.
privacy.016: FileDesk’s use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
privacy.018: Connection details remain locally until you disconnect. Temporary network errors do not delete accounts. Choosing Disconnect removes that account’s local login credentials. Downloaded files and cloud originals are not deleted and remain under your control.
privacy.019: You can also revoke FileDesk access in Google Account third-party connections. Provider policies, security measures or revoked permissions may require signing in again. Since the operator does not store cloud files on its servers, delete those files on your device or through the provider.
privacy.021: If you email support, your supplied email address and message are used to answer your inquiry. Do not send passwords, authentication tokens or sensitive file content. Request deletion of correspondence at the same address. This website uses no advertising or behavioral-analytics scripts or tracking cookies. The hosting provider may process access logs, including IP addresses, to serve and secure pages.
privacy.022: Update checks. Once a day, or when you choose Check for Updates, FileDesk makes one anonymous GitHub API request for the latest public version. It includes no account, cookie or file data, only a User-Agent containing the app version. GitHub may process access logs such as IP addresses. Turn off Automatically Check for Updates in the FileDesk menu to disable automatic requests.
privacy.024: If data handling changes, this page and its update date will be revised. Providers may request additional consent if permissions change. For privacy inquiries: FileDesk, ifreemumu@gmail.com.
